live.name: NICKEL KIMBALL
live.headline: NICKEL KIMBALL: a threat actor tracked under many names
live.in_short: NICKEL KIMBALL is the Secureworks name for an actor also known as Kimsuky and APT43. The catalogue lists its aliases and tools. No public report in this library describes its operations.

sentences.t: NICKEL KIMBALL is the name Secureworks uses for this threat actor.
Other vendors track it under many other names, including APT43, Kimsuky, Emerald Sleet, Velvet Chollima, THALLIUM, TA427 and Black Banshee.
The catalogue lists eight tools tied to the actor: BabyShark, FastFire, FastSpy, FireViewer, KONNI, KimJongRAT, Kimsuky and ReconShark.
No public report in this library describes its operations.

next.name: NICKEL KIMBALL
next.headline: NICKEL KIMBALL (Kimsuky): a spying group aimed mostly at South Korea, per vendor reports
next.in_short: NICKEL KIMBALL is tracked under many names, including Kimsuky and APT43. Vendors link it to North Korea. Reports describe phishing, Android spyware and fake-document lures aimed mostly at South Korean targets. Attribution varies by report.

sentences.t: The catalogue lists NICKEL KIMBALL under many aliases, including Kimsuky, APT43, Emerald Sleet, Velvet Chollima, THALLIUM and TA427.
BleepingComputer's report on Microsoft's findings calls Kimsuky a North Korean state actor, also known as Emerald Sleet or Velvet Chollima.
ESRC linked a February 2022 malicious Word document to Thallium, also known as Kimsuky. The report describes the actor as North Korea-linked.
Sekoia and Kudelski Security say some DPRK experts regard Kimsuky as a mega-cluster with several branches, such as TA406 and TA408. The report adds that vendors name and divide clusters differently.

Where Kimsuky ends and other groups begin is disputed. Genians says some researchers class KONNI, Kimsuky and APT37 as one group, and that they overlap in targets and infrastructure. It cites an MSMT report that treats Kimsuky and KONNI as distinct.
DCSO says KONNI is generally understood to fall under the Kimsuky cluster of DPRK Reconnaissance General Bureau-linked actors.
